ref_atoms.ref_content: DMA enabled memory range registers are configured & locked prior to starting any DMA operation. Range registers may be configured by OT firmware at boot time and locked from further modification until next reset.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Describes the locking mechanism of DMA enabled memory range registers, a specific hardware feature to prevent reconfiguration during operation.

ref_atoms.ref_content: If the configured source address space ID is SOC (CTN or System) and destination address space ID is OT internal, then destination address pointer must lie within the DMA enabled memory range.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Specifies a precise address checking rule based on source/destination address space IDs, verifiable via access violation tests.

ref_atoms.ref_content: If the configured destination address space ID is SOC (CTN or System) and source address space ID is OT internal, then source address pointer must lie within the DMA enabled memory range.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Specifies a precise address checking rule for opposite direction, verifiable via access violation tests.

ref_atoms.ref_content: If source (or destination) address space ID is set to CTN, then read (or write transactions) are sent to CTN port only. If CTN port is configured to be 32 bits, then make sure that the upper 32 bits of the source (or destination) address register pointer are all zeroes.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Defines CTN port routing and a specific address alignment check for 32-bit CTN configuration, testable via transaction monitoring and address value checks.

ref_atoms.ref_content: If source (or destination) address space ID is set to OT Internal, then read (or write transactions) are sent to OT internal port only. Make sure that the upper 32 bits of the source (or destination) address register pointer are all zeroes.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Defines OT internal port routing and address alignment, verifiable via transaction monitoring and address value checks.

ref_atoms.ref_content: If source (or destination) address space ID is set to System, then read (or write transactions) are sent to system port only. Full 64 bits of the source (or destination) address pointer is available.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Defines system port routing and full 64-bit address usage, verifiable via port routing checks.

ref_atoms.ref_content: When Hardware handshake enable is set to 1 and Go bit is set, the DMA engines start listening to input interrupt for hardware handshake operation.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Describes the combined effect of control bits that activate interrupt listening in hardware handshake mode, testable by observing DMA behavior after configuration.

ref_atoms.ref_content: In hardware handshake receive mode (Data Direction = 0), upon interrupt assertion from the low speed IO peripheral indicating FIFO threshold, the DMA engine reads 'total size' number of bytes from the source address (FIFO) and writes them to the destination buffer, with each read width equal to 'transfer width'. The source and destination addresses are updated according to the auto-increment enable settings.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Defines the exact data movement behavior in receive hardware handshake mode, including trigger, transfer size, width, and address update dependency, all of which are directly testable.

ref_atoms.ref_content: In hardware handshake transmit mode (Data Direction = 1), upon interrupt assertion from the low speed IO peripheral indicating FIFO almost empty, the DMA engine reads 'total size' number of bytes from the source buffer and writes them to the destination address (FIFO), with each write width equal to 'transfer width'. The source and destination addresses are updated according to the auto-increment enable settings.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Defines the exact data movement behavior in transmit hardware handshake mode, including trigger, transfer size, width, and address update dependency, testable via functional tests.

ref_atoms.ref_content: FIFO address auto-increment enable: If set, consecutive 'transfer width' worth of data chunks are popped from the FIFO using consecutive register addresses; if not enabled, consecutive data chunks are popped by repeatedly reading the same register address. For writes (transmit), if set, consecutive 'transfer width' worth of data chunks are pushed to the FIFO using consecutive register addresses; if not enabled, data is written to the same register address. When enabled and the FIFO depth is reached, the FIFO address wraps back to the start address. Data buffer Auto-increment Enable: If set, data shall be loaded into consecutive buffer segments in memory, where each segment is equivalent to 'total size' worth of data. The Destination address (in receive) or Source address (in transmit) register is incremented by 'Total Size' once an equivalent amount of data is emptied/filled. If not set, the same buffer segment is overwritten or re-read each time a hardware handshake operation is triggered. All combinations of the two increment enable bits are allowed, and their interaction governs the address behavior as detailed in the appendix.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Describes the detailed behavior of FIFO and data buffer auto-increment controls that determine address generation and buffer reuse, critical for data integrity verification in hardware handshake modes.

ref_atoms.ref_content: DMA controller enforces the following data movement rules based on address space identifiers: OT Private Memory can only send data to OT Private Memory or OT DMA Memory, not to SoC Memory; OT DMA Memory can send to all; SoC Memory cannot send to OT Private Memory but can send to OT DMA Memory or SoC Memory.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Specifies hardware-enforced data movement permissions between address spaces, defining which transfers are allowed and which are forbidden, testable via illegal access attempts.

ref_atoms.ref_content: DMA controller provides status registers that can be polled to track operation completion, and generates a completion interrupt upon finishing a DMA operation.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Indicates the existence of status registers and completion interrupt as hardware mechanisms observable during verification.
